acceptance: The owner's choice is recorded on this item before any code change.
The chosen behaviour is evidenced through both tpcds and tpcds_obt entry points, not from a raw binary run alone.
A scale factor is refused as a whole only if the owner chose option (d) and approved the number.
context: Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).
description:
## Problem
dsqgen builds a full key permutation for query 9's `ulist(random(1, rowcount("store_sales")/5, uniform), 5)`. Measured on darwin-arm64 (dsqgen sha256 3225615e13a2..., seed 19620718): SF 3000 3.4-5.1 s, SF 5000 11.1-13.4 s, SF 7000 and 10000 killed at 45 s (2.5 and 3.6 GiB), SF 100000 killed above 14 GiB. Query 1 at SF 100000 takes 0.2 s; query 9 is the only template with this construct. The earlier item (tpcds-dsqgen-q9-timeout-sf10000-20261111) was closed against a 3000 cap the owner did not approve; this item replaces it.

## Change
Options, none preselected: (a) no change, query 9 times out as before; (b) fail only query 9 generation early above an owner-approved scale with the cost-growth reason, leaving data generation and the other 98 queries working; (c) generate query 9's five parameters without the full permutation, with a design and numbers shown first; (d) a scale-wide maximum at an owner-approved number, which needs CLI, MCP, API and site tests and a breaking changelog entry (the owner's 2026-11-17 answer allowed lowering 'to the largest scale that works' if query 9 'cannot be fixed quickly'); (e) a longer query 9 timeout.

## Decision gates
Blocked until the owner chooses among (a) to (e). Before asking, measure query 9 uncapped (no 45 s kill) at SF 5000, 6000, 7000 and 10000 through `make heavy-run` on darwin-arm64 and, if a Linux host is available, linux-x86_64: time, peak RSS and dsqgen sha256; the owner approves those runs first. The 5000 in this item's id is not a chosen threshold: 5000 to 7000 is unmeasured. For (b) the owner approves the exact scale before it is committed. For (c) the owner approves the design before code merges; a kit patch changes the dsqgen digest and needs separate approval. A scale-wide limit only under option (d) with the owner's number.

## Verification rubric
Pass for (b): query 9 above the approved scale fails fast with the reason through tpcds and tpcds_obt entry points, both tested; every other query and dsdgen data generation at that scale are unaffected, shown by test. Pass for (c): generated SQL for query 9 matches dsqgen output at scales where dsqgen works, for at least three seeds.

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label id or text is shown to the owner before it is committed. Briefs quote owner answers verbatim; questions to the owner carry no preselected answer.
- The implementer replies on review threads and leaves resolving them to the reviewer or the owner, unless the owner says otherwise (AGENTS.md asks agents to resolve benchbox-oracle threads on soundness paths; the owner has been asked which applies).
- Hosted writes (merge, close, disable or enable auto-merge, workflow dispatch, remote branch delete) only as the repository's close-out procedure or the owner's word for that pull request allows; never raw `gh pr merge` in core.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted. Push only after `make pr-preflight` exits 0 on the exact head.
- No worktree takeover while another session may be working; no tracker write from a server that reports a stale version; never chain `git stash` with `git stash pop`.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point, one run at a time.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
